title: Choose a record class, record struct or conventional class from equality, copying and inheritance requirements, and predict what generated equality and `with` copies do with reference members

options: `True`, because `with` starts from a copy of `a` and the new array holds the same element
`False`, because `b` is a separate record object, so it does not share its identity with `a`
`False`, because `a.Tags` and `b.Tags` are different array instances that compare by reference
`True`, because `Order` is a record, so generated equality compares its data instead of identity

rubric.point: Chooses `False` because the two records hold different array instances, and generated record equality compares the `Tags` member with the array's reference equality.

questions.model: `False`, because `a.Tags` and `b.Tags` are different array instances that compare by reference. The `with` expression replaced the copied array reference with a new array. Generated record equality compares each member with that member type's own equality, so the arrays are unequal even though they hold the same element.

questions.prompt:
A C# geometry library needs a type for a 2D grid cell holding two `int` coordinates. Cells are created in very large numbers inside tight loops and used as `Dictionary` keys. Two cells with the same coordinates must compare equal, a cell must never change after creation, no other type will inherit from it, and a missing cell is never represented as `null`.

Which of `record class`, `record struct`, `readonly record struct` or a conventional `class` fits best? Give the choice and the reason it beats the closest alternative.

rubric.point: Gives a valid reason over the closest alternative: e.g. versus `record class`, no inheritance or null is needed so a small value type avoids a heap object per cell; or versus plain `record struct`, `readonly` makes the positional properties init-only so the cell cannot be mutated (which also keeps it safe as a dictionary key).

questions.model: `readonly record struct`. It gives generated value equality like a record class, but nothing here needs inheritance or `null`, so a small value type avoids allocating a heap object per cell; and unlike a plain `record struct`, its positional properties are init-only, so a cell cannot be mutated after creation.

c2.text: readonly record struct since inheritence not needed so struct fit, the objects with the same properties are equal from struct, and it will never change because readonly, no null because of struct as well which will always contain default value

c1.feedback: The answer is “`False`, because `a.Tags` and `b.Tags` are different array instances that compare by reference”.

annotations.note: This is the right choice for a small, immutable, equality-based key type.

annotations.quote: inheritence not needed so struct fit
annotations.note: You tied the lack of inheritance to choosing a struct, which is a valid reason over `record class`.

annotations.quote: it will never change because readonly
annotations.note: You said `readonly` prevents mutation, which is the reason it beats a plain `record struct`. This also makes the cell safe as a dictionary key.

annotations.quote: no null because of struct as well which will always contain default value
annotations.note: Correct extra point: a struct is never `null` and defaults to zeroed fields, which matches the requirement that a missing cell is never `null`.

c2.feedback: You chose `readonly record struct` and justified it against both `record class` (no inheritance or null needed) and plain `record struct` (`readonly` prevents mutation).
